reviews.body:
`cancel()` already does this for a plain query that has been sent but is not `sent[0]`: it calls `quiet(x)` and then waits on `x.cancel`. `cancelBatch` took the same branch without starting that timer, so a `sql.batch` stuck behind a long query never settled even with `cancel_timeout` set.

Calling `quiet(x)` before returning the promise matches the existing path, and `quiet()` is a no-op when `cancel_timeout` is unset or a timer is already running. The new unit test (batch queued behind a simulated sleep, then `cancel()` under a 0.1s timeout) is the case that was hanging.
